text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd plans to cut back services from Australia to Taiwan, reducing both its flight frequency and the size of the aircraft used.
"It's a matter of fine tuning the service to the market," a Qantas spokesman said.
Qantas has flown five flights a week to Taipei with two 310-seat Boeing 747SPs, an old model of the jumbo jet that achieved longer range by having a shorter fuselage.
The spokesman said Qantas had replaced the 747SPs with 228-seat Boeing 767-300ERs. From next month, the frequency would fall to four flights a week.
The 747SPs were now flying between Melbourne and Hong Kong, boosting capacity on that route, he said.
Demand on the Taiwan route was growing but the rate of growth had slowed and by re-allocating the aircraft, the airline would reduce the number of of empty seats.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
